rules.title: Permitted Upfront Payments and Maximum Security Deposit
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or agent cannot require a tenant to pay any amount exceeding first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to the first month's rent, and the purchase and installation cost for a key and lock.
rules.key_value: First month's rent, last month's rent, security deposit equal to 1 month's rent, plus key and lock costs
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property leases and tenancies at or prior to commencement.
rules.exemptions: Leases, rentals, occupancies, or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span:
At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
(i) rent for the first full month of occupancy;  and,
(ii) rent for the last full month of occupancy calculated at the same rate as the first month;  and,
(iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)
rules.conflict_note: The document contains two versions of clause (1)(b)'s introductory text: one effective until August 1, 2025, and an amended version effective August 1, 2025.

rules.title: Statement of Condition Requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent accepting a security deposit must provide the tenant, upon receipt or within 10 days after commencement of tenancy (whichever is later), a separate written statement of the existing condition of the premises, including all existing damage and code violations, containing a mandatory 12-point bold-face disclosure.
rules.key_value: Within 10 days after commencement of tenancy or upon receipt, whichever is later
rules.coverage_conditions: Lessors of residential real property or their agents who accept a security deposit.
rules.exemptions: Leases, rentals, occupancies, or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: Any lessor of residential real property, or his agent, who accepts a security deposit from a tenant or prospective tenant shall, upon receipt of such security deposit, or within ten days after commencement of the tenancy, whichever is later, furnish to such tenant or prospective tenant a separate written statement of the present condition of the premises to be leased or rented.

rules.title: Security Deposit Holding in Separate Bank Account
rules.requirement: Security deposits must be deposited into a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank within Massachusetts beyond the reach of creditors, and the landlord must provide a receipt with bank details within 30 days of receiving the deposit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Security deposits received by lessors of residential real property.
rules.exemptions: Leases, rentals, occupancies, or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth under such terms as will place such deposit beyond the claim of creditors of the lessor, including a foreclosing mortgagee or trustee in bankruptcy, and as will provide for its transfer to a subsequent owner of said property.  A receipt shall be given to the tenant within thirty days after such deposit is received by the lessor which receipt shall indicate the name and location of the bank in which the security deposit has been deposited and the amount and account number of said deposit.

rules.title: Annual Interest on Security Deposits
rules.requirement: A landlord who holds a security deposit for one year or longer must pay interest annually at the rate of 5% per year, or the lesser amount actually received from the bank, beginning from the first day of tenancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies where the landlord holds a security deposit for one year or longer.
rules.exemptions: Leases, rentals, occupancies, or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy.

rules.title: Return of Security Deposit and Allowable Deductions
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the security deposit or remaining balance within 30 days after tenancy termination; deductions are restricted solely to unpaid rent or water charges, certain tax escalation increases, and reasonable repair costs for tenant damage beyond reasonable wear and tear backed by a sworn itemized list.
rules.coverage_conditions: Termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of a tenancy under a valid written lease.
rules.exemptions: Leases, rentals, occupancies, or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.interaction: Deductions for unpaid rent or water charges must not have been validly withheld or deducted pursuant to any general or special law; tax escalation clauses must conform to section 15C.
rules.quoted_span:
The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof;  provided, however, that the lessor may deduct from such security deposit for the following:
(i) any unpaid rent or water charges which have not been validly withheld or deducted pursuant to any general or special law
(ii) any unpaid increase in real estate taxes which the tenant is obligated to pay pursuant to a tax escalation clause which conforms to the requirements of section fifteen C;  and
(iii) a reasonable amount necessary to repair any damage caused to the dwelling unit by the tenant or any person under the tenant's control or on the premises with the tenant's consent, reasonable wear and tear excluded.

rules.title: Treble Damages for Security Deposit Violations
rules.requirement: If a landlord fails to place the security deposit into a compliant bank account, fails to transfer it properly upon sale or transfer of the property, or fails to return the deposit or balance within 30 days of termination, the tenant is entitled to three times the deposit amount plus 5% interest, court costs, and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: Three times the security deposit amount plus 5% interest
rules.coverage_conditions: Failure by the lessor or his agent to comply with clauses (a), (d), or (e) of subsection 6.
rules.exemptions: Leases, rentals, occupancies, or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: If the lessor or his agent fails to comply with clauses (a), (d), or (e) of subsection 6, the tenant shall be awarded damages in an amount equal to three times the amount of such security deposit or balance thereof to which the tenant is entitled plus interest at the rate of five per cent from the date when such payment became due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
